reason: The cited evidence does not address the effect of Co removal on SFE, nor does it compare the dynamic behavior of Co-free FeNiCrMn with CoCrFeMnNi. E1 discusses strain hardening and dynamic recovery in a different context, E2 notes limited high-strain-rate data for HEAs, and E3 mentions general strengthening mechanisms in the Cantor alloy without supporting the specific SFE-twinning-dislocation mechanism proposed.
premises: Co removal increases SFE relative to CoCrFeMnNi
Higher SFE reduces deformation twinning and favors dislocation glide
Under dynamic loading, this shift causes more rapid dislocation multiplication and enhanced interactions
Enhanced dislocation interactions increase dynamic strain hardening and strain-rate sensitivity
The Co-free alloy will show higher dynamic yield strength and lower twin volume fraction than the baseline
